name: Scaffold
description:
A the Gray Zone theater company in Racine that performs original works in whatever space is available — abandoned buildings, public parks, factory floors, and once on a moving freight train (the audience rode in the next car). Scaffold doesn't have a permanent venue; instead, each production is site-specific, written for and performed in a space that becomes part of the story. The company's founder, a playwright named Yael Nkomo-Lindgren, believes that theater divorced from real space is just television, and that the audience should never be comfortable enough to forget they're in an actual place with actual walls and actual weather.

Scaffold's productions run the spectrum from gritty social realism to surrealist nightmare, and they've built a reputation for work that makes audiences genuinely uncomfortable — not through shock, but through proximity. When Scaffold stages a play about the Gray Zone poverty, they stage it in an actual the Gray Zone apartment. When they write about industrial labor, they perform in a working factory during off-hours. The actors are not trained professionals; they're the Gray Zone residents who audition and rehearse around day jobs, and their performances have a raw, unpracticed quality that Yael considers a feature, not a bug. Productions are free. Donations are accepted. The company survives on grants from the Milwaukee Cultural Collective and on Yael's apparently inexhaustible willingness to do this for no money.
